title: The Hoary Frost, the Fleecy Snow
description: The Hoary Frost, the Fleecy Snow in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 866 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Winter”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The hoa-ry frost, the flee-cy snow, De-scend, and clothe the ground; The liq-uid streams for-bear to flow, In i-cy fet-ters bound.

lines: The hoary frost, the fleecy snow,
The liquid streams forbear to flow,
When, from his dreadful stores on high,
The man that does his power defy
God sends his word and melts the snow;
He calls the warmer gales to blow,
The changing wind, the flying cloud,
With songs and honors sounding loud,

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
